programme.desc: In Detroit, a cunning serial killer (Matthew Fox) pushes young detective and psychologist Alex Cross (Tyler Perry) to his moral and psychological limits.

programme.desc: Stranded on a mountain after a plane crash, two strangers must work together to survive the extreme elements of the remote, snow-covered terrain. Realizing that help is not on the way, they embark on a perilous journey across hundreds of miles.

programme.title: Shazam! Fury of the Gods

programme.title: History: The Interesting Bits
programme.sub-title: How to Get Away with It
programme.desc: A look at some of history's criminals, con artists, frauds and fakes, from Adam Worth, the 19th-century inspiration for Professor Moriarty, to a jewel thief named Diamond Doris and a count who sold the Eiffel Tower to gullible buyers twice.

programme.title: History: The Interesting Bits
programme.desc: A look at espionage; meeting spies from Delilah to Roald Dahl and along the way revealing the real model for James Bond.

programme.title: History: The Interesting Bits
programme.desc: A look at wars that lasted for centuries and others that were over in minutes, as well as the difficulty of ending a war; the possibility of starting a war over almost anything, from an unprovoked invasion to a lost ear, a pastry or a stolen bucket.

programme.title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
programme.desc: The reasons to study the ancient Greeks; their iconic art and architecture, philosophy, religion and inventions of drama and democracy; the Greeks in cultural, historical and linguistic terms; the development and character of Greek civilization.

programme.title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
programme.sub-title: Bronze Age Greece: Minoans and Myceneans
programme.desc: Human habitation on the mainland and islands of Greece; the Bronze Age cultures of the Cycladic islands; the Minoan civilization centered on Crete; the Mycenaean civilization and its monumental architecture; Mycenae's connection with the Trojan War.

programme.title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
programme.desc: Greece's Dark Age is an era of restricted trade and a breakdown of centralized power; the achievements of this epoch include iron technology, the Greek alphabet and the Olympic Games; Greece's geographical expansion; creation of city-states.

programme.title: The Greek World: A Study of History and Culture
programme.sub-title: Classical Greece: The Age of Pericles
programme.desc: Greece's Classical Age is an astonishing period of human accomplishment; defining events of the period; the 479 B.C.E. defeat of the Persians; the period of the Peloponnesian War; the emergence of Macedonia as a great power; Alexander's exploits.

programme.title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
programme.desc: Contemplating the French art de vivre and the appeal that makes France one of the most visited tourist spots; an overview of the upcoming journey across the rich cultural landscape of France; learning about the iconic figure of Charles de Gaulle.

programme.title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
programme.sub-title: The Birth and Rise of Paris
programme.desc: Learning how Paris evolves from an ancient settlement to a Roman city and then the capital; studying medieval Paris through the Cluny Museum, the great cathedral of Notre Dame and the royal chapel of Sainte-Chapelle; following the growth of Paris.

programme.title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
programme.desc: Discovering the Palace of Versailles as the world of Louis XIV; noting how the landscaping surrounding the palace symbolizes features of Louis's reign and how the Versailles court prizes royal spectacle; exploring Louis's patronage of the arts.

programme.title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
programme.desc: Examining the social and political background of the French Revolution of 1789; visiting key locations in Paris where the events unfold, from a coffee house to the site of the Bastille prison and the Place de la Concorde; mapping Napoleon's rise.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.desc: A framework for an exploration of Jewish influences on Jesus; being a Jew in the ancient world; Jewish temples; similarities between Judaism and other ancient religions.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.sub-title: Sacred Mountains and Law Giving in Judaism
programme.desc: There is little distinction between religion and politics in ancient Judaism; the importance of the law in Jewish religion; the connections between the giving of the law to Moses on Mount Sinai and the Sermon on the Mount.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.sub-title: The United and Divided Israelite Kingdoms
programme.desc: A look at the kingdoms of David and Solomon; the transformation of 12 Israelite tribes into a monarchy; how it is crumbling over tensions regarding how to properly worship the God of Israel; probing controversies.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.desc: The end of the First Temple Period; examining the reign of King Josiah; his popular religious reforms reassert the importance of Jerusalem's Temple; the Temple's traumatic destruction; its relationship to Gospel accounts and the Second Temple.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.desc: The Babylonian exile ends; the returning exiles began to re-establish themselves in Jerusalem under Ezra and Nehemiah; this leads to a dramatic schism between Jews and Samaritans; encounters with Samaritans.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.sub-title: The Jewish Diaspora and the Golden Rule
programme.desc: Insights into the ancient Jewish diaspora communities; close readings of the Book of Tobit and the Book of Esther; insights into the directions from books about holiness and the treatment of other people; a historical literary debate.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.sub-title: Alexander the Great's Impact on the Jews
programme.desc: Alexander the Great's visit to Jerusalem and Judea; his influence on the development of ancient Jewish traditions; examining possible narrative parallels between these two iconic figures of Western history.

programme.title: Jesus and His Jewish Influences
programme.sub-title: Jews and Greek Rule: The Heliodorus Affair
programme.desc: The Heliodorus Affair; the power struggle between Jerusalem's elite families during the time of the Ptolemies and Seleucids; how it is a key turning point in the history of Jews in Judea; echoes of this conflict in Gospel accounts of taxation.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.sub-title: From Jesus to the Creation of the Church
programme.desc: In the early days of the Christian faith, there is no church; no single institution to guide the followers of Jesus; stepping into the world of the early church; the roots of Christianity as found in ancient Jewish traditions and the gospel.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.desc: In the first century A.D., the followers of Christ evolve from a band of disciples into tight-knit communities of worship; a glimpse of these communities in some of the earliest Christian documents; the Acts of the Apostles and the letters of Paul.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.desc: Christianity quickly spreads all over the Mediterranean region in the first few centuries; learning how believers adapt the practice of their faith to create a great diversity of worship in the early church.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.desc: The Christian church catches the attention of the Roman emperor; he views the faithful as a threat to imperial authority and Roman culture; the widespread persecution of Christians that follows; a new class of Christian heroes, the martyred saints.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.desc: In 312 A.D., Christianity gains a powerful ally when the Roman emperor Constantine adopts the faith of Jesus as his own; seeing how this shift affects Christian believers; the church goes from being a persecuted minority to a privileged minority.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.desc: Freed from Roman persecution, the church undergoes an institutional revolution; a unified doctrine that is still recognizable in today's Catholic Church; the impact of these changes; a church hierarchy; the establishment of orthodox beliefs.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.desc: Christianity becomes the chief religion of Rome; Latin overtakes Greek in the West as the premiere language of the faith; the rich developments of Latin church theology; the earliest thinkers; an important father of Christian theology, Augustine.

programme.title: The Catholic Church: A History
programme.sub-title: Popes and Bishops in the Early Middle Ages
programme.desc: Christian society is thrown into turmoil by the fall of Roman authority; citizens are left prey to Germanic tribes; the church provides leadership in the chaos that follows; consolidating power for its chief officials, the pope and the bishops.
